data.name: Workshop.Req.Tpm.Pass
data.value: TPM {0} is present.

data.name: Workshop.Req.Tpm.FailMissing
data.value: Windows does not find a TPM. Check in the BIOS/UEFI whether a firmware TPM (Intel PTT, AMD fTPM) is turned off.

data.name: Workshop.Req.Tpm.FailVersion
data.value: The TPM is only version {0}; Windows 11 requires TPM 2.0.

data.name: Workshop.Req.Tpm.FailDisabled
data.value: The TPM is disabled in the BIOS/UEFI. Enabling it meets the requirement.

data.name: Workshop.Req.Tpm.Unknown
data.value: The TPM state is unknown (not fully readable without administrator rights).

data.name: Workshop.Req.Graphics.NotChecked
data.value: DirectX 12 support and a WDDM 2.0 driver were not checked.

data.name: Workshop.Data.Nothing
data.value: There is no usable hardware data.

data.name: Workshop.Data.Incomplete
data.value: Some sources could not be read ({0}); the affected results are marked as unknown.

data.name: Workshop.Data.NotElevated
data.value: Bootrix runs without administrator rights. TPM state, BitLocker and Secure Boot can only partly be determined that way. Run the analysis as administrator for a complete result.

data.name: Workshop.Cpu.NoModernInstructions
data.value: The processor lacks {0}. According to community reports Windows 11 from version 24H2 does not start on such processors (not confirmed by Microsoft); bypassing the Setup checks does not change that. Windows 10 22H2 with extended security updates, or Linux, is therefore recommended.

data.name: Workshop.Cpu.Arm64
data.value: Arm64 device: the image must be for Arm64. Drivers for Wi-Fi, storage and touch usually come only from the device maker, and x64 tools only run through emulation.

data.name: Workshop.Cpu.Arm32
data.value: This device has a 32-bit Arm processor; there is no Windows installation media for it.

data.name: Workshop.Cpu.Only32Bit
data.value: The processor can only run 32-bit code. Windows 11 is not possible; Windows 10 22H2 (x86) is the last Windows version for it.

data.name: Workshop.Cpu.Running32Bit
data.value: A 32-bit Windows is running on this 64-bit capable processor. An x64 image is recommended for the reinstallation.

data.name: Workshop.Cpu.NewPlatform
data.value: The processor "{0}" probably belongs to the new Arm platform that Microsoft scoped Windows 11 26H1 to. Older versions may not include the platform support (a hint, not confirmed); if in doubt, use the image from the device maker.

data.name: Workshop.Boot.SecureBootSignedOnly
data.value: Secure Boot is on: only media whose boot manager the firmware accepts will start. FAT32 with Microsoft's original boot manager is recommended instead of NTFS with an additional boot loader.

data.name: Workshop.Boot.Certificate2023
data.value: The firmware has revoked the Windows Production PCA 2011: only boot managers signed with the Windows UEFI CA 2023 start. The medium must contain such a boot manager.

data.name: Workshop.Boot.Certificate2011
data.value: The firmware does not know the Windows UEFI CA 2023 yet: only a boot manager with the previous signature (Windows Production PCA 2011) starts.

data.name: Workshop.Boot.BiosMode
data.value: The system boots in BIOS mode: the medium gets an MBR partition table.

data.name: Workshop.Boot.BiosLargeDisk
data.value: In BIOS mode with MBR only 2 TB of a disk can be used; "{0}" is larger. Large disks need UEFI with GPT.

data.name: Workshop.Licensing.EditionFromFirmware
data.value: The license key in the firmware belongs to the edition "{0}". Windows Setup selects that edition by itself with the key.

data.name: Workshop.Licensing.EditionFromRunning
data.value: The edition of the running Windows ("{0}") is suggested; no firmware key confirms it.

data.name: Workshop.Licensing.EditionUnknown
data.value: The device has a license key in the firmware, but its edition could not be determined unambiguously.

data.name: Workshop.Licensing.NoFirmwareKey
data.value: No license key found in the firmware. The running Windows can still have a digital license.

data.name: Workshop.BitLocker.Active
data.value: BitLocker is active or suspended on {0}. Back up the recovery key before reinstalling; it is requested after changes to firmware or boot order.

data.name: Workshop.BitLocker.Locked
data.value: Drive {0} is locked by BitLocker. Without the recovery key the data cannot be read.

data.name: Workshop.BitLocker.Unknown
data.value: The BitLocker status is unknown (administrator rights needed).

data.name: Workshop.Machine.Virtual
data.value: This is a virtual machine ({0}). TPM, Secure Boot and firmware mode depend on how the VM is configured.

data.name: Workshop.Machine.HyperVGeneration1
data.value: Hyper-V generation 1 VM (BIOS): Windows 11 is meant for a generation 2 VM with UEFI and a virtual TPM.

data.name: Workshop.Machine.ServerHardware
data.value: The device is server hardware. RAID and network drivers come from the server maker; have its driver pack ready. Vendors usually do not certify server hardware for Windows 11.

data.name: Workshop.Machine.RunningServer
data.value: A Windows Server is currently running on the device.

data.name: Workshop.Storage.NoDisk
data.value: No internal disk was detected. In Windows PE a storage driver may be missing.

data.name: Workshop.Lifecycle.RunningVersionEnding
data.value: {0} end of servicing: {1:d} (Home and Pro).

data.name: Workshop.Windows10.EndOfSupport
data.value: Windows 10 22H2 has had no regular support since 14 October 2025. According to Microsoft, extended security updates (ESU) for consumers run until 12 October 2027 and require enrollment; terms may vary by region.

data.name: Workshop.Alternative.Windows10
data.value: Alternative with Microsoft support: Windows 10 22H2 with extended security updates (ESU).

data.name: Workshop.Alternative.Linux
data.value: Alternative: a current Linux distribution; it also runs on older hardware and is updated continuously.

data.name: Workshop.Bypass.Unsupported
data.value: A Windows 11 with bypassed Setup checks is not supported by Microsoft; updates are not guaranteed.

data.name: Workshop.Driver.IntelVmd
data.value: Intel Volume Management Device "{0}" ({1}): without the Intel RST/VMD driver (iaStorVD), Windows Setup may find no drives. Add the driver to the Setup medium.

data.name: Workshop.Driver.IntelRstRaid
data.value: The storage controller "{0}" ({1}) runs in RAID mode (Intel RST). Without the Intel RST driver Windows Setup may find no drives. Add the driver, or switch the BIOS to AHCI before a reinstallation (an existing installation will no longer start afterwards).

data.name: Workshop.Driver.AmdRaid
data.value: The storage controller "{0}" ({1}) runs in AMD RAID mode. Without the AMD RAID driver Windows Setup may find no drives.

data.name: Workshop.Driver.HardwareRaid
data.value: RAID controller "{0}" ({1}): have the manufacturer's driver ready; Windows does not include one for every controller.

data.name: Workshop.Driver.VirtualStorage
data.value: Virtual storage controller "{0}" ({1}): Windows includes no driver for it. Load it in Setup (virtio-win or the VMware driver) or choose another controller type.

data.name: Workshop.Driver.NetworkNoDriver
data.value: No working driver is installed for the network adapter "{0}" ({1}) at the moment (error code {2}). Provide the driver for the reinstallation.

data.name: Workshop.Driver.NetworkVendor
data.value: The network adapter "{0}" ({1}) uses a driver from {2} that is not part of Windows. It may be missing in Setup or the first-run experience; back up the drivers of this PC.

data.name: Workshop.Driver.NetworkVirtual
data.value: Virtual network adapter "{0}" ({1}): Windows includes no driver for it (virtio-win or VMware Tools).

data.name: Workshop.Driver.WirelessNoDriver
data.value: No working driver is installed for the Wi-Fi adapter "{0}" ({1}) at the moment (error code {2}). Provide the driver for the reinstallation.

data.name: Workshop.Driver.WirelessVendor
data.value: The Wi-Fi adapter "{0}" ({1}) uses a driver from {2} that is not part of Windows. It may be missing in Setup or the first-run experience; back up the drivers of this PC.

data.name: Workshop.Capture.SecretsIncluded
data.value: The capture contains secrets in clear text (keys and passwords). Store it encrypted only, and do not print or log it.

data.name: Workshop.Capture.WlanExportFiles
data.value: The exported Wi-Fi profiles in "{0}" contain the keys in clear text. Delete the files as soon as they have been taken over.

data.name: Workshop.Capture.WlanKeysProtected
data.value: For {0} Wi-Fi profiles the key could not be read in clear text (administrator rights needed).

data.name: Workshop.Capture.ProductKeyMayBeGeneric
data.value: The Windows key read from the registry can be a generic installation key when the license is digital; it is then not usable on other hardware.

data.name: Workshop.Capture.RecoveryKeyUnavailable
data.value: No recovery password could be read for {0} (drive locked, no password protector or missing rights).

data.name: Error.ElevationDenied.Cause
data.value: Administrator permission was not granted.

data.name: Error.ElevationDenied.Action
data.value: Confirm the Windows User Account Control prompt so that disks can be read and written.

data.name: Error.BrokerStartFailed.Cause
data.value: The elevated Bootrix process could not be started ({0}).

data.name: Error.BrokerStartFailed.Action
data.value: Restart Bootrix. If the problem persists, start Bootrix with "Run as administrator".

data.name: Error.BrokerDisconnected.Cause
data.value: The connection to the elevated Bootrix process was lost.

data.name: Error.BrokerDisconnected.Action
data.value: Check the disk before using it: a running write was aborted. Repeat the operation.

data.name: Error.BrokerProtocol.Cause
data.value: Communication with the elevated Bootrix process failed ({0}).

data.name: Error.BrokerProtocol.Action
data.value: Close all Bootrix windows and start the program again.

data.name: Error.MediaWriterUnavailable.Cause
data.value: This version of Bootrix has no way to write this image ({0}) yet ({1}).

data.name: Error.MediaWriterUnavailable.Action
data.value: Try the "Write image byte for byte (DD)" mode if the image is suited for it.

data.name: Error.AnswerFileExists.Cause
data.value: The image already contains an answer file (autounattend.xml) that the job says must not be replaced.

data.name: Error.AnswerFileExists.Action
data.value: Allow replacing it (the original is kept as autounattend.xml.original) or drop the options that need an answer file.

data.name: Error.DriverFolderRejected.Cause
data.value: The driver folder "{0}" cannot be used: {1}

data.name: Error.DriverFolderRejected.Action
data.value: Choose a folder that contains only unpacked drivers (.inf, .sys, .cat), no programs and no links.

data.name: Error.DriverInjectionFailed.Cause
data.value: None of the {0} drivers could be added to the Windows image ({1}).

data.name: Error.DriverInjectionFailed.Action
data.value: Check that the drivers are signed and match the architecture of the image. The $WinPEDriver$ folder on the medium still holds them.

data.name: Error.BootManager2023Unavailable.Cause
data.value: This Windows image has no boot files signed with the Windows UEFI CA 2023 (build {0}): {1}

data.name: Error.BootManager2023Unavailable.Action
data.value: Use a current Windows 11 image (25H2 or newer) or choose the previous signature (Windows Production PCA 2011).

data.name: Error.BootManager2023Unverified.Cause
data.value: The replaced boot files do not carry the Windows UEFI CA 2023 signature: {0}. The original files were restored.

data.name: Error.BootManager2023Unverified.Action
data.value: Use an unmodified original image from Microsoft or choose the previous signature (Windows Production PCA 2011).
